question: What Caraga freshwater evidence is available in the 2026 Agusan Marsh Puntius binotatus reproductive study, and does its public abstract support site-level occurrence or a species inventory?

source.citation: Sularte, R. P., & Jumawan, J. C. (2026). Ovary morphology and histological studies of the female Spotted barb Puntius binotatus (Valenciennes, 1842) from Agusan Marsh, Agusan del Sur, Northeastern Mindanao Islands, Philippines. Iranian Journal of Ichthyology, 13(2), 108-115. https://doi.org/10.22034/iji.v13i2.1161
source.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, as stated on the publisher's article page.

abstractClaims.studyFocus: Female ovary morphology and histology; the abstract reports mature ovaries and active spawning during a dry sampling month.

access.publisherAbstract: The official publisher-indexed article record supplied the title, citation, abstract, named waterbodies, aggregate count, reproductive summary and license.
access.fullText: The publisher article page could not be opened by the web reader (cache miss), and a direct read-only page request timed out after 15 seconds. No PDF or access control was bypassed.
access.limitations: The full methods, sampling dates/month, per-waterbody sample counts, taxon-to-site crosswalk, voucher accessions, coordinates, sampling gear and source images were not retrieved.

interpretation.safeSummary: The publisher abstract reports a pooled sample of 158 P. binotatus collected across the named Lake Tugno, Lake Panlabuhan and Agusan River study area and summarizes female reproductive histology. It is a one-taxon reproductive study, not a multi-species fish inventory.
interpretation.siteResolution: The abstract gives no per-site count or explicit specimen-to-waterbody allocation. Do not create three separate lake/river presence records from the pooled statement.
notSupported: A complete fish species list for Agusan Marsh or any of its lakes and rivers.
Independent P. binotatus occurrence records at each of the three named waterbodies.
A precise collection month, seasonality pattern beyond the abstract wording, station coordinate, or mapped waterbody geometry.
Natural diet, bait guidance, catchability, abundance trend, current water safety or fishing rules.
Reproduction or spawning behavior for populations outside the study's unspecified pooled sampling context.

decision.reason: The abstract is a useful recent Caraga research lead, but the site crosswalk and methods are unavailable and the study covers one reproductive taxon rather than regional inventory coverage.

nextAction: Continue searching for accessible Caraga primary fish inventories with explicit site-level evidence. Revisit this article's full methods and any specimen-to-site detail if the publisher page becomes normally retrievable; keep the abstract summary research-only meanwhile.

references.supports: Official article title, DOI, abstract, study locations, aggregate specimen count, reproductive summary and CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license.
Official journal issue listing identifies volume 13, issue 2 as the June 2026 issue and lists this article on pages 108-115.
